bole.text: Trunk used for timber in Ecuador and Peru; bark decoction used as a red dye (vernacular names 'sangre de toro', 'llora sangre').

crown.text: Not described by a source read.

phenology.fruit: globose to subglobose capsule 2.0-3.0 x 1.5-2.0 cm, apex mucronate; aril white-yellow

bark.text: Not described; used for a red dye.

habitat.range: north-central Venezuela to central Bolivia; highest-reaching American Myristicaceae (to 2500 m)

notes: Jaramillo-Vivanco & Balslev 2020 revision (src 0, read as Plazi XML; partial treatment): lamina 8-26 x 3-11 cm, petiole 15-30 mm winged, 8-14 secondary veins per side; no height, bark colour, flower colour or phenology in the text. Holotype label: 'flood-free rainforest' at 150 m (Maranon); 'simple' leaf implied by lamina/petiole, not stated. Vela-Apaza 2024 (src 1): present in the Madre de Dios river floodplain plots Cocha Lobo and Jacaratia (seasonally flooded) but nearly absent from the Los Amigos plots; patchy/clumped. Search snippets cited herbarium labels (tree 17-28 m, fruit green turning red) but those NYBG pages were not readable, so not entered. No frugivore source found.

sources.title: Jaramillo-Vivanco & Balslev 2020, Revision of Otoba (Myristicaceae), Phytotaxa 441(2):143-175, doi 10.11646/phytotaxa.441.2.3 (Plazi treatment XML)
